title: Minaret of Jam
summary: The Minaret of Jam is a 65 m brick tower in a mountain river valley in Ghur province, Afghanistan. An inscription dates it to 1194 and names the Ghurid sultan Ghiyas ud-Din; it was probably built to commemorate his 1192 victory at Delhi. It is covered in elaborate brickwork and became a UNESCO World Heritage site.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS reports an inscription giving 1194 as the date of construction. End is the present: the minaret still stands.

reviewer_note: Shape tower. ICOMOS: 65 m high from a 9 m diameter octagonal base, four tapering cylindrical shafts, fired brick; UNESCO repeats 65 m. 1194 is the inscription date reported by ICOMOS; the 1192 victory is ICOMOS's 'likely' reading. The 9 m is the octagonal base's diameter, not the shaft's.
